summary_en: Japan Engine Corporation raised its full-year earnings forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027, with net profit expected to rise 10.0% to 5,510 million yen. The interim dividend was set at 30 yen per share as previously announced, and the year-end dividend forecast was raised by 11 yen to 81 yen per share, bringing the full-year dividend to 111 yen, up 23 yen from the prior fiscal year's 88 yen.
title_en: Notice Regarding Upward Revision of Full-Year Business Forecast and Interim Dividend and Revision to Year-End Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
Japan Engine Corporation has revised its full-year earnings forecast upward for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, with net profit expected to increase 10.0 percent to 5,510 million yen from the previous projection of 5,010 million yen. Operating profit is forecast to rise 8.2 percent to 6,360 million yen, and net sales to grow 4.0 percent to 34,000 million yen.

In conjunction with the earnings upgrade, the company raised its dividend forecast. The interim dividend, already announced at 30 yen per share with a record date of September 30, 2026, remains unchanged. The year-end dividend forecast was increased by 11 yen to 81 yen per share. Combined with the interim distribution, the full-year dividend per share is now projected at 111 yen, representing a 23-yen increase from the prior fiscal year's 88 yen per share.

The company attributed the improved outlook to favorable trends in the new shipbuilding market and steady global expansion of its UE engine. The marine diesel engine business is progressing well with the first hydrogen-fuel engine unit on track for delivery within the fiscal year. The repair and parts business has benefited from robust maintenance parts sales amid high vessel utilization rates, and from expanding profit cycles among Chinese licensees, which have increased production capacity and output volumes beyond original expectations, driving higher royalty and parts supply revenues.
